p: Festival Place is the heart of modern Basingstoke, but walk a few minutes south and you'll find the Top of Town, the old market area with the Willis Museum on Market Place. It's a free local museum with displays on the town's history and a few surprises, and it's a nice quieter contrast to the shopping centre.

Right next to Festival Place, Eastrop Park is a handy spot for a run-around, with a play area, open lawns and a paddling pool in the summer months. War Memorial Park, a little further into town, is another lovely green space with mature trees and a bandstand.

Basingstoke has a famous literary neighbour. Jane Austen was born in the village of Steventon, just outside the town, and Jane Austen's House at Chawton, near Alton, is the cottage where she lived and wrote. It's a short drive and a lovely visit for fans of her novels.

History buffs will enjoy Basing House in Old Basing, the ruins of a huge Tudor palace that was besieged during the English Civil War. The Vyne, a National Trust house near Sherborne St John, has grand rooms, gardens and woodland walks.
For a bit of the countryside, the North Wessex Downs are within reach, with great walking country and views across Hampshire.
The good news is that a lot of these options are easy to combine with a session at Flip Out, so you can mix energy-burning with something a bit more relaxed and give everyone a day to remember.
